accuracy.evidence: Definitions checked: biodiversity counts the variety of species, not individuals (monoculture = low biodiversity); endangered = at serious risk of extinction, extinct = no individuals left anywhere, dodo last recorded in the 1600s (IUCN Red List categories; Natural History Museum on the dodo); habitat loss is the largest driver of wildlife decline (WWF Living Planet Report 2024); fossil fuels formed over millions of years from ancient organisms and are non-renewable, sunlight/wind/moving water renewable (BBC Bitesize KS2 and KS3 energy resources); a carbon footprint is total greenhouse-gas emissions caused by a person's activities in kg CO₂e. Travel numbers from UK DESNZ 2023 conversion factors: average car 0.166 kg CO₂e/km, local bus 0.102 kg per passenger km, so a 4 km day is 0.66 ≈ 0.7 kg and 0.41 ≈ 0.4 kg as the lab shows. Replanting is presented as slow ('Trees take many years to grow back'), not instant. Parameterised answers checked at corners: p2 a−b 12..20/3..9 (≥3), p4 k*4, m6 r*w, m10 t−c 15..30/4..12 (≥3).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented KS2 confusions: many individuals of one plant counted as high biodiversity (step 1 prediction 'The field: it has more plants', tag 'many', p1), animals simply move to the remaining trees (step 2 prediction, tag 'move'), litter away from water is harmless (step 3 prediction 'It stays where it was dropped', m5), coal is renewable because it came from plants (step 4 prediction, wrong-bin feedback, tag 'coal', m8), carbon footprint read literally or as rubbish (step 5 prediction, tags 'literal' and 'rubbish', m2) and endangered vs extinct (tag 'endang', p5, m4).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagenvimp is built from this topic's own vocabulary: a species-count comparison of a wood and a wheat monoculture, a tree-cutting model where tree-dependent species leave at set thresholds and return on replanting, a litter-and-rain model where unbinned litter is washed into the river and fish fall by 2 per piece, a renewable/non-renewable sort of six named sources, and a five-day school-trip planner that totals kg of CO₂ from DESNZ factors and scales a footprint. It is unrelated to flagimpact (impact of words on others) and ecolab (food webs), and the 6-shingle gate is under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child sees each word's meaning before it is named: the counters show wood 8 vs field 1 after tapping 8 different organisms and many identical wheat plants; the 'Kinds of animal' counter drops from 5 to 2 as trees fall and climbs back on replanting; fish disappear only when rain washes un-binned litter in; wrong-bin drops explain why coal is non-renewable; the week total falls from 3.5 kg to under 1.75 kg only when car days change to bus or walking. Each task ends with a one-line definition of the term just shown.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'The field: it has more plants' (the field counts 1 kind), 'They move into the trees that are left' (owl, squirrel and woodpecker leave as trees go), litter 'stays where it was dropped' (rain carries it into the river), coal renewable because 'plants grow back' (the bin rejects it with the millions-of-years reason), and carbon footprint as 'How far you walk' (walking makes it 0 kg).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven feedback messages keyed to the slip: 'many' (kinds, not numbers), 'move' (remaining trees are full; habitat loss), 'coal' (fossil fuels formed over millions of years), 'literal' and 'rubbish' (it counts carbon dioxide gas), 'endang' (endangered = few left, extinct = none, never back) and 'car' (burning fuel vs walking, what sustainable means). In-lab messages name each slip too: which animal left and why, the fossil-fuel reason for a wrong sort, and how much each travel choice adds.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes the family kid limit (FK ≤ 5.0 + 0.5) and the adult limit (FK ≤ 10.0 + 0.5) after the adult text was rewritten from FK 11.2 into shorter sentences. All twelve topic terms are used in their precise meaning and each is defined in a short kid sentence (habitat, deforestation, endangered, extinct, pollution, fossil fuel, renewable, carbon footprint, sustainability, conservation). Canvas labels are 11–18 px dark ink on white pills.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes after replacing 'journey' in the family tip with 'trip'. Every kid paragraph defines terms with an example; adult paragraphs give the definitions with sources, the renewable/fossil-fuel and footprint definitions, then the named mistakes with the exact travel factors the lab uses. No repeated template text across the six steps.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at iPhone 13 (390 px) in light and dark after Show me on every step. Fixes made from them: sorted energy cards overlapped inside the bins ('wind' hidden under 'moving water'), so sorted items now stack as emoji + left-aligned label rows; the unsorted cards sit in two rows of three; the feather icon for the woodpecker was replaced by a bird with a name label under every animal; the footprint shape was too small to read and now scales from a larger base beside the kg readout. Buttons use the 56 px young-learner size.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: count each organism by name, Cut a tree/Plant a tree, '→ bin' per litter item and Make it rain, pick an energy source then → Renewable/→ Non-renewable, and one button per day that cycles car/bus/walk with an aria-label naming the current choice. tell() updates the canvas aria-label and the visible description on each change. walk.cjs on desktop and iPhone 13 completed all 5 tasks, showed the challenge, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in either theme with no console errors.
